# Preface {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note}
**Written by AI, not yet reviewed by a person.** Drafted by Claude (Anthropic) on 2026-10-19 from the maintainer's
direction for this book (fishycode plan 033). Reviewed by: nobody yet.
:::

Since 2013 the ICES Working Group on Spatial Fisheries Data (WGSFD) has worked out how to turn vessel tracks and
fishing records into maps of fishing effort, pressure on the seabed, and catch. Two workshops, WKSSFGEO (2021) and
WKSSFGEO2 (2023), took the work to small-scale fleets, which often carry no VMS and keep no logbook. The thinking is in
thirteen reports, some 1,300 pages, written one meeting at a time. Few people have read them all; most of us have read
the ones we were in the room for.

This book gathers that work in one place, ordered by the problem rather than by the meeting.

- **Its centre is one flow, drawn as a diagram** in the first chapter. Each ping gets its vessel, its trip, its
  record, its gear, whether it was fishing, its effort and its share of the catch. Each comes from the best source the
  data offer, with a fallback when that source is missing, and a note of which source answered.
- **Each chapter starts from what the groups wrote**, cited by report and page. Then it sets out the problem, the ways
  others have approached it, and code that does it.

The code is [ramb](https://github.com/einarhjorleifsson/ramb), an R package for that flow. Its examples run on public
data: the workshops' own example sets, which ship with ramb. The Icelandic data that fishycode builds appear as
background, one country's data among others, used where they show something the public sets cannot.

The book is for the members of WGSFD and WKSSFGEO, and for anyone joining the work. It is young: most of its chapters
are still to be written, and the groups will, with luck, keep giving it more to say.
